about: Flags of football federations of another day that flag-icons does not have (docs/design/football-years.md, 'Federations of the day'). Each is a public-domain SVG from Wikimedia Commons, read 2026-11-09 from the file page named (robots.txt allows /wiki/ pages and upload.wikimedia.org), committed under scripts/data/historic-flags/ and redrawn on flag-icons' 4:3 canvas (640 x 480) by npm run build:historic-flags, which writes public/flags/<file>.svg; --check rebuilds them byte for byte. The redrawing keeps every path of the original: the flag is scaled by its height to 480 and cut to 640 wide, at the fly for a flag whose emblem sits in the canton, evenly on both sides for a centred one; a plain field is redrawn as rectangles in the new coordinates. sha256 is the original as served by upload.wikimedia.org, lfSha256 the committed snapshot (git keeps text with LF line endings).

flags.name: Soviet Union
flags.licence: Public domain: not an object of copyright under article 1259 of Book IV of the Civil Code of the Russian Federation (Commons: PD-RU-exempt), as the file page states

flags.name: Yugoslavia (SFR Yugoslavia)
flags.licence: Public domain: ineligible for copyright (simple geometry, official insignia) and expired under Yugoslav copyright law (Commons: PD-ineligible, PD-shape, PD-Yugoslavia), as the file page states

flags.name: FR Yugoslavia, then Serbia and Montenegro
flags.licence: Public domain: an official act of state authorities under the copyright law of Serbia and Montenegro, and ineligible for copyright (Commons: PD-SerbiaGov, PD-ineligible), as the file page states

flags.name: Zaire
flags.licence: Public domain: an official act, and expired under Ordinance-Law No. 86-033 of 5 April 1986 of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (Commons: PD-Congo), as the file page states

flags.name: CIS (the flag of its team at Euro 1992)
flags.licence: Public domain: simple geometric shapes and text, below the threshold of originality (Commons: PD-textlogo), as the file page states
